summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia and a history of COPD and recurrent pneumonias, was admitted for respiratory distress, hypotension, and altered mental status. She was initially managed in the ICU with IV antibiotics, a norepinephrine drip, and a central line due to hypotension and severe hypoxia. Imaging confirmed right lower lobe pneumonia with possible pleural effusion. Her condition improved rapidly with nebulized treatments and antibiotics. She was weaned off vasopressors, transitioned to oral levofloxacin, and started on a prednisone taper. Anxiety was noted to exacerbate her dyspnea. She remained stable, was discharged home with service, and instructed to complete her antibiotic and steroid courses, continue home medications, and reduce her nicotine patch dose.
